records.label: Seven members of two families

phenotypes.text: bilateral symmetrical putaminal lucencies on CT

quotes: A unique disorder is described in seven members of two families in whom dystonia was variably associated with subacute visual loss or asymptomatic optic atrophy, and striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen.

records.label: Kindred with Leber's disease and dystonia
records.segregation: Mode of inheritance compatible with maternal transmission
quotes: We studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease; 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration; and 1 had both disorders.
The mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission.

records.label: Five-generation Hispanic family

variants.as_reported: G-to-A transition at nucleotide pair (np) 14459 ... alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72

records.segregation: Six maternal relatives in three generations harbored the mutation; one female with LHON was heteroplasmic
quotes: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions was studied.
One of these variants, a G-to-A transition at nucleotide pair (np) 14459, changed a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72.
Six maternal relatives in three generations were tested and were found to harbor the mutation, with one female affected with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy being heteroplasmic.

records.label: Large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia

phenotypes.text: severe complex I deficiency in muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

variants.as_reported: T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene (isoleucine 26 to methionine)
A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene (valine 312 to isoleucine)

quotes: A rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) that is associated with hereditary spastic dystonia has been studied in a large Dutch family. Neuropathy and ophthalmological lesions were present together in some family members, whereas only one type of abnormality was found in others.
A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.
A second mutation, a homoplasmic T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene, resulted in the substitution of a methionine for the isoleucine at amino acid residue 26.

records.label: Japanese family
records.onset: dystonia in childhood; optic neuropathy late onset
quotes: We investigated a Japanese family with generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, which occurred in childhood, and late-onset optic neuropathy.
We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese, by estimating the frequency of each nucleotide change.
The significance of the A3203G mutation remains unknown.

records.label: LHON and spastic dystonia family

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

quotes: A pathogenic 3697G>A/ND1 mutation was detected and seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.
The 3697G>A/ND1 mitochondrial DNA mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype in the same family.
To report a novel mutation that is associated with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) within the same family affected by spastic dystonia.

records.label: Chinese LDYT family
records.segregation: Homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side
quotes: we describe a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients
revealed a mutation (mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A)) substituting a threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 of MTND3 on the background of haplogroup D4b
Quantitative analysis of the heteroplasmy of the mutation revealed a homoplasmy in the leukocytes of all the affected individuals on the maternal side.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2009) used resequencing microarray analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome to identify a homoplasmic m.10197G>A mutation in MTND3, resulting in an ala47-to-thr substitution at a highly conserved residue, on a haplogroup D4b background in a Chinese family with 18 patients with LDYT. This was the first description of an ND3 mutation causing LDYT.
quotes: revealed a mutation (mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A)) substituting a threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 of MTND3 on the background of haplogroup D4b
This is the first description of the ND3 mutation causing LDYT.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2009) noted that the m.10197G>A mutation in MTND3 had also been reported in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome, and suggested that the clinical presentations associated with this mutation are much wider, encompassing both LDYT and Leigh syndrome.
quotes: The mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A) mutation has recently been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.
These findings suggest that the clinical presentations associated with the mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A) mutation (ND3) are much wider, encompassing those of LDYT and Leigh syndrome.

notes.statement: Wang et al. (2009) stated that LDYT, a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia, had been known to be caused by mutations in the mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 genes, and showed that it can also be caused by mutation in ND3.
quotes: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.
This is the first description of the ND3 mutation causing LDYT.

notes.statement: Spruijt et al. (2007) screened the complete mitochondrial DNA of a patient with LHON who lacked the 3 primary LHON mutations and identified a pathogenic 3697G>A mutation in the ND1 gene, which seemed to be associated with isolated complex I deficiency. The authors concluded that the mutation caused both LHON and spastic dystonia in the same family.
quotes: The complete mitochondrial DNA was screened for mutations in a patient with LHON without 1 of these 3 primary mutations.
A pathogenic 3697G>A/ND1 mutation was detected and seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.

notes.statement: Spruijt et al. (2007) noted that the 3697G>A ND1 mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome, and suggested that other genetic factors may contribute to the clinical expression. The family's clinical features resembled those of previously described families with LHON and dystonia due to an ND6 mutation.
quotes: This mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome (which encompasses mitochondrial myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke), and other genetic factors may contribute to the clinical expression.
This family has similar clinical characteristics as the previously described families with LHON and dystonia with an ND6 mutation.

notes.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) sequenced the entire mtDNA of the proband from a Japanese family with childhood-onset generalized dystonia and late-onset optic neuropathy. They found 42 nucleotide changes compared with the revised Cambridge reference sequence. Two of these, A3203G and G14459A (in ND6), were absent from 200 healthy Japanese controls. The significance of A3203G remained unknown.
quotes: The mtDNA of the proband showed a total of 42 nucleotide changes.
We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese, by estimating the frequency of each nucleotide change.
To our knowledge, this is the first case of LHON with dystonia that revealed a mtDNA mutation in a Japanese family.

notes.statement: In a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia, De Vries et al. (1996) found none of the mtDNA mutations previously reported in LHON; sequencing of the protein-coding mitochondrial genes identified a heteroplasmic 11696A-G transition in ND4 (val312-to-ile) and a homoplasmic 14596T-A transition in ND6 (ile26-to-met).
quotes: mtDNA mutations previously reported in LHON were not present. Sequence analysis of the protein-coding mitochondrial genes revealed two previously unreported mtDNA mutations.

notes.statement: De Vries et al. (1996) found severe complex I deficiency in a muscle biopsy from the family, which they suggested linked the mtDNA mutations to the complex phenotype including Leber optic neuropathy.
quotes: Biochemical analysis of a muscle biopsy revealed a severe complex I deficiency, providing a link between these unique mtDNA mutations and this rare, complex phenotype including Leber optic neuropathy.

notes.statement: Jun et al. (1994) found that the np 14459 variant was absent from 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs and from 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, and 99 African mtDNAs; the family's mtDNA was of Native American haplogroup D.
quotes: The np 14459 variant was not found in any of 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs, nor was it detected in 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, or 99 African mtDNAs.
The mtDNA proved to be a Native American haplogroup D genotype

notes.statement: Jun et al. (1994) concluded that because the np 14459 G-to-A missense mutation was family-specific, altered a moderately conserved amino acid in a complex I gene, was unique among haplogroup D mtDNAs, and was heteroplasmic, it was likely the disease-causing mutation.
quotes: Thus, the np 14459 G-to-A missense mutation is specific to this family, alters a moderately conserved amino acid in a complex I gene, is a unique mtDNA variant in Native American haplogroup D, and is heteroplasmic, suggesting that it is the disease-causing mutation.

notes.statement: Miyoshi et al. (1969) reported a familial form of holotopistic striatal necrosis.
quotes: Familial holotopistic striatal necrosis.

notes.statement: Novotny et al. (1986) found that the mode of inheritance in a kindred with Leber optic neuropathy and dystonia was compatible with maternal transmission. They suggested that the disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.
quotes: The mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission.
This neurologic disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.

notes.statement: Marsden et al. (1986) suggested that the disorder might be a variant of Leigh disease but noted considerable differences from pathologically proven Leigh disease, and stated that it must be excluded in all patients thought to have idiopathic dystonia, subacute visual failure similar to Leber optic neuropathy, or a combination of these.
quotes: It is possible that this is a variant of Leigh's disease. However, there were considerable differences between these patients and those with pathologically proven Leigh's disease.
This condition must be excluded in all patients thought to have idiopathic dystonia, subacute visual failure similar to Leber's optic neuropathy, or a combination of these disorders.
